title: Stability Stitch: Ops sprint curation and evening oncall pulse
content:
Purpose and audience:
- Quick operational snapshot for the SRE rotation (evening pulse) and a compact plan for the next sprint (2 weeks). Intended for on-call engineers and SRE leads.

High-level summary (afternoon check, 2027-01-18 16:30 PT):
- No active P0s. One elevated P1 latency cluster observed in eu-west for the hosted API between 02:20–03:10 UTC (early-local morning). Impact contained via fallback routing at ~02:36 UTC.
- Error budget burn for the last 7 days: 3.2% (target monthly burn < 8%).
- Recent changes: runtime kernel selection tweak deployed to canary (pr #892) — currently in rollout to 10% of traffic.

Incident digest (eu-west latency spike — brief):
- Symptom: p95 latency for text-generation rose from baseline 210ms to ~760ms for ~48 minutes. Token-level latency spike (decoder step) observed.
- Detection: automated latency alert (p95 > 500ms sustained 10m) tripped and created a PagerDuty incident.
- Immediate mitigation taken:
  - Automatic route failover engaged (traffic shifted to eu-central and us-west for new requests).
  - Small pre-warmed pool of dedicated instances (reserved pool) spun up manually by oncall at 02:40 UTC.
- Root-cause hypothesis (working): delayed autoscale from cloud provider + KV cache pressure causing more cold starts and slower kernel path selection on older GPU instances.
- Evidence:
  - Autoscale logs show scale-trigger queueing starting 02:18 UTC with container spin-up latencies 70–120s (higher than typical 12–20s).
  - Runtime telemetry shows increased cache-miss ratio and a higher proportion of the slower attention kernel selected under the observed sequence length distribution.
  - No related infra maint windows or provider incidents recorded during the timeframe.
- Short-term actions:
  - (A1) Increase eu-west reserved warm pool by +3 instances during high-risk hours (nights) — ticket JIRA-OPS-1247.
  - (A2) Add autoscale alarm to notify earlier at 60% CPU + queue depth (currently 80%) to give pre-warm headroom.
  - (A3) Roll back any model-variant promotion in eu-west if kernel-swap correlates further with latency.
- Long-term follow-ups:
  - (L1) Experiment: pre-warm strategy vs lower autoscale threshold — measure cost delta and tail latency improvement over 2 weeks (experiment doc link in linked_artifacts).
  - (L2) Runtime change: add a lightweight KV-prefetch heuristic for common prefixes to reduce cold KV cache misses (RFC queued).

SLO status and interpretation:
- SLOs monitored: 95th latency < 300ms (global), availability (5xx) < 0.2% over rolling 30d.
- Current snapshot (rolling 30d): latency p95 = 268ms (within SLO), availability = 0.13% (within SLO).
- Actionable observation: the recent eu-west spike produced a narrow blip but did not push the 30d window over the threshold.
- Recommendation: keep alert sensitivity the same for latency but add region-specific sticky alerts so eu-west can be addressed without global escalations if cross-region failover is in place.

Handoff script for evening -> night oncall (template – paste into Slack channel):
- Status: "GREEN" / no P0. One P1 (eu-west latency) investigated; mitigations in place.
- Incidents to watch: eu-west autoscale headroom (ticket JIRA-OPS-1247).
- What I changed: increased canary percentage of kernel-selection tweak to 10% (PR #892), added manual warm pool of +3 eu-west instances (temp).
- Standard runbooks to open: runtime-latency-troubleshoot, autoscaler-debug, routing-fallback (links in pinned channel).
- Who to escalate to: Marco Liu (infra), Priya Desai (runtime), Platform Pager (escalation group).
- Key metric dashboards: latency-p95-global, eu-west-autoscale-queue, kv-cache-hitratio.

Ops experiments and measurement plan (next 2 weeks):
- Experiment A: Lower autoscale threshold for eu-west from 80%->65% with identical warm pool size. Hypothesis: lower threshold reduces cold-start tail latency but increases baseline cost by ~5–8%. Metric: mean p95 latency, cost delta per hour.
- Experiment B: Implement KV-prefetch heuristics in canary (5% traffic). Hypothesis: prefetch reduces cache-miss rate and decoder-step latency for repeated prompt prefixes. Metric: cache-miss ratio, p99 token-step time.
- Experiment C: Controlled batching policy — increase batching window by +10ms on low-latency-critical routes to see batching benefit vs added end-to-end latency. Metric: tokens/sec and p95 latency.
- Gate for rollback: any experiment that increases availability error rate > 0.05% absolute in 1h window -> immediate rollback.

Action items (owners and ETA):
- Nadia: finalize autoscale alert tweak + create JIRA change request (ETA: 2027-01-19 EOD).
- Marco: provision +3 reserved instances in eu-west and enable cost tracking label (ETA: 2027-01-19 10:00 UTC).
- Priya: run the KV-prefetch RFC and schedule a 5% canary (ETA: RFC review 2027-01-21).
- Evan: extend canary monitoring to include token-step histograms (ETA: 2027-01-20 morning).

Notes to the next oncall (short):
- If latency spike recurs, do immediate cross-region diversion and notify Platform Pager. Use warm-pool manual growth if autoscale lags.
- Keep an eye on PR #892 canary metrics — if token-step tail increases, rollback.
- Report any unexpected cost spike in the reserved pool to finance channel (tag: cost-ops).

Retro snippet (what we learned this sprint):
- Our fallback routing and runbooks worked as intended — failover contained wider impact.
- Autoscale latency remains the most likely vector for tails; proactive warm pools and earlier alerting materially reduce impact.
- Need better provider SLAs on container spin-up or an internal fast-path for critical routes.

Appendix: quick links and runbook crumbs
- Runbooks: runtime-latency-troubleshoot | autoscaler-debug | routing-fallback
- Important tickets: JIRA-OPS-1247 (reserved pool), JIRA-OPS-1259 (kv-prefetch RFC)
- Canary traces: trace-id sample (eu-west spike) = trace_20270118_euw_09a3f

End of note.
